A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphDO study and contain readable methods, equations, results, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. The appendices match completely; v5's additional page reflects reference reflow rather than additional research.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments on six graph tasks, including accuracy comparisons in Tables 1–2, additional experiments in Figures 6–7 and model-response cases in Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 6–7, together with the model-response cases in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendix A retain the same graph encoder, BFS/DFS/PR/PPR ordering procedures, task-specific personalization vectors and prompting methods. No algorithm, model or inference component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six graph tasks using GraphDO's synthetic graphs and CORA, Citeseer and Pubmed subgraphs. The represented domains and ego/forest-fire sampling coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: random order, BFS, DFS, PR and PPR in Tables 1–2; shortest/longest path orders alongside retained comparators in Figure 6; and the same model/order comparisons in Figure 7.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–C retain the same models, prompt styles, accuracy metric, zero decoding temperature, graph counts, generation and sampling parameters, and response-evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The across-order sensitivity analysis in Figure 4, answer-overlap experiment and model study in Section 5, and success/error cases in Appendix D are all retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix C reports three repetitions for node-classification experiments in both versions. There are no changes to repeated-run disclosures, uncertainty reporting, seed information or significance testing.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings and appendix cases are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains mean connectivity accuracy of 89.43% for BFS versus 78.36% for random order, and Table 2 retains 82.67% for PR on Pubmed with ego sampling.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation, graph encoding definition, PR/PPR expressions, personalization-vector definitions and across-order variance formula are unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is added, removed or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about ordered descriptions improving graph reasoning, task-dependent sensitivity and the GraphDO contribution. The added code-availability sentence does not change these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the attention-bias hypothesis, task-specific mechanism explanations, answer-overlap interpretation and case-study explanations. The limitations concerning unexplored graph structures and the absence of rigorous theoretical explanations are also unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds an explicit GraphDO code-repository link in the abstract, absent from v4. Implementation, hardware, hyperparameter and data-processing disclosures in Appendices A–C are unchanged. The supplied PDFs establish the new access information but not repository usability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and referenced works remain the same. The SLANG reference is updated from its arXiv preprint to its EMNLP 2024 publication, including an author-name correction; this bibliographic update leaves research positioning unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 revises affiliation/contact information, adds affiliation and corresponding-author footnotes, adds funding acknowledgements and the abstract's code sentence, and makes small typographical and bibliographic edits. The scientific narrative and section sequence remain essentially identical.

P2.justification: The revised author block, added footnotes and acknowledgements change text flow and reference pagination. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–5 retain their designs, captions and contents. The appendix pages are visually identical at their shifted PDF positions.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves reproducibility information by providing an explicit GraphDO code link, and improves documentation through funding disclosure and corrected reference metadata. The scientific evidence and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged. The benefit is limited to documentation and implementation discoverability; repository usability cannot be established from the PDFs.
